chapter: Georgie Auld, Hawkins and Los Angeles
title: Joining Coleman Hawkins; catching up on Minton's repertoire
summary: Pettiford introduces him to Hawkins, who hires him; McGhee has to learn Monk's tunes and the bebop melodies at Minton's.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: in... He was going with Hawk, and Hawk was going to California, and I heard about it, so he asked me was I interested, and I told him "Damn right." I wanted to get to California, because December here in New York wasn't too cool! I said, "Yeah, I'd love to be out in California." So anyway, he introduced me to Hawk, and Hawk asked me would I consider joining his band -- and he told me what he band. So I said, "Yeah, okay."

And I joined his group, and I... He hipped me to a lot of music, because I didn't know... The things I'd been playing with big band, nobody was using those, not on 52nd Street anyway... They wasn't using those particular tunes and so forth and so on, so I had to get hip to what Monk's tunes were and whatever else they was playing up at Minton's. So that's when I started hanging out up at Minton's, to find out what was happening with the music.
Who did you hang out with up there? Who was up there mostly?

Well, Kenny Clarke. And I would go up there with Dizzy; sometimes we'd go up and play. And I had the chops in the range, so I had no problem as with what they would play. But I didn't know the tunes. Like, the melodies that they used on "Stompin' At The Savoy" and the other tunes. They had different melodies for them than the
melody that I knew. But I knew the changes, all the chord changes and all of that, which was a help regarding those -- I didn't know where I was at!
But all the cats used to come up there. Like, Prez used to come by there all the time. And ain't no tellin'... I loved Prez anyway. Wherever he was, I'd go find him, you know.
